Subject: DeltaBridge integration: post-call action items — SDK/auth/rerankers & prompt governance

Hi Samir / Anita —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our discovery call so everyone has a single source of truth. I tried to keep this actionable.

What we covered (short):
- Primary use case: customer support triage + automated suggested responses; candidate pipeline enrichment via resume parsing + reranking.
- Data flow: user transcripts -> embeddings index -> retrieval -> LLM generation + optional reranker.
- Non-negotiables: PII controls, audit logs, and predictable latency for 95th pct.

Immediate asks / owners:
1) SDK & auth: provide example flows for both API-key and mTLS in our SDKs; include sample code for token rotation. Owner: Aditya (we agreed to share an SDK example and a small repo). Due: Tue 6/15.
2) Routing & deployment: show routing policy options (latency-first vs cost-first) and default fallbacks. Owner: Camila. Due: Wed 6/16.
3) Structured output & tool-calling: deliver a recommendation for JSON schemas + function/tool calling pattern that preserves auditability. Owner: Lauren. Due: Fri 6/18.
4) Embeddings/re-ranker: propose embedding dimensions, index type, and a simple reranker architecture for short-form responses. Owner: DeltaBridge (Samir) + Redwood engineering review. Due: Fri 6/18.
5) Prompt governance & security: outline versioning, injection mitigations, and a red-team plan. Owner: Marissa (security + evaluations). Due: Mon 6/21.

Attachments: I uploaded the sketched architecture we drew during the call (delta-bridge-arch-v1.pdf) and a first-pass prompt template list (sample-prompt-templates.md).

Next immediate step: Aditya will drop an SDK snippet and auth options by Monday morning (6/14 PST) so you can validate.

Thanks — talk soon.

—

Hi Samir — quick technical response on the auth/SDK side.

Auth options we support (short):
- API Key (bearer): simplest, supports key rotation via our Console + KMS. Good for hosted API use.
- OAuth2 (client_credentials): supported for partner integrations; good if you want token scoping per service.
- mTLS: supported on Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments. mTLS is available with VPC/private install for mutually authenticated endpoints.

So: you can run mTLS if you go Dedicated/private; hosted customers typically use API keys or OAuth. If you want hybrid (mTLS at edge + hosted backend), we can discuss a gateway pattern.

SDK snippet (node, minimal):
```
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ endpoint: 'https://api.redwood.com/v1', apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY });
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-base', prompt: 'Summarize ticket:' });
```
(Full examples + rotation script in sdk-auth-examples.zip attached.)

Routing & fallback: you can configure route policies by tag: {region: 'us-west', cost_tier: 'low', latency_slo_ms: 150}. The runtime will fallback to a compatible quantized variant if capacity is constrained. Camila will share policy templates.

Embeddings & reranker baseline advice:
- Embedding dims: 1024 common tradeoff for mid-latency retrieval.
- Index type: HNSW is a good first step.
- Reranker approach: lexical filter -> semantic similarity -> lightweight learned reranker (score fusion).
- Targets for short-form support: aim for recall@10 >= 0.85 and top-1 accuracy (after reranker) >= 0.65 for first 3 months; tune from there.

I'll push the examples and a small test repo link to the Drive (see related_links). Happy to hop on a quick sync if you want to review the code.

—Aditya
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya — that's helpful. A couple security items before we proceed with a trial: 

1) Prompt injection mitigations: can you outline default sandboxing/escaping strategies, and whether Redwood supports a prompt allowlist/denylist at the API layer? We need to prove we can prevent outbound PII leakage if a prompt contains malformed user-provided content.

2) Red-team plan: we'd expect a sequence (initial audit -> threat model -> attack run -> fixes -> re-test) and a place to store evidence. Would Redwood run the red-team or supply tooling & templates for our platform team?

If you have a sample prompt template that includes system prompts + schema enforcement for structured outputs (to avoid hallucinated fields), that would be very helpful.

Best,

Hi Anita / Samir — jumping in with the prompt governance + red-team plan we discussed offline. High level:

Prompt governance (proposed):
- Prompt versioning: store canonical prompts in a Git repo with semantic tags (e.g., v1.0-system-intent). Each production rollout pins a prompt commit hash in the model route config.
- Prompt templates: enforce structured-output schemas using function-calling + JSON schema validation at the application layer; samples attached (sample-prompt-templates.md).
- Injection mitigations: multi-layer checks — input sanitizer (strip unprintable/escape control sequences), model-side guardrails (system prompt with denylist + instruction to refuse), and post-generation schema validation + blacklist filters. We keep a private "prompt-blacklist" file in Drive for audit.
- Red-team cadence: initial baseline audit (internal) -> 2-week targeted attacks (external contractors) -> fix window (2 weeks) -> re-test. We produce an evidence bundle (logs, failed prompts, remediation steps) and store in your Drive folder for compliance.

Action items & owners:
- Marissa: deliver governance doc + red-team template + evaluation harness (pytest style) by Mon 6/21.
- Aditya: finalize SDK examples for mTLS + rotation by Tue 6/15.
- Camila: routing policy examples by Wed 6/16.
- Lauren: schema recommendations and function-calling patterns by Fri 6/18.

Procurement note: I see procurement@deltabridge copied — once you confirm the model/policy choices we'll share a concise SOW. For audit purposes we'll also include SOC2 questionnaire answers (SOC2-questionnaire.xlsx attached).

If helpful, I'll set a 30min technical follow-up early next week to walk through the sample prompts + the evaluation harness.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Head of Security + Evaluations, Redwood Inference
